::: {.callout-important}
## Summary

- **A new orthology reference covers all six SATURN species:**
  - *Mnemiopsis*, oyster, fly, *Ciona*, zebrafish, human;
  - plus the choanoflagellate *Salpingoeca rosetta* as an outgroup, to root the tree.
- **The outgroup fixed the missing Metazoa level.** The 4-species run of [Oct 15](2026-10-15-saturn-orthofinder-orthogroups-vs-eggnog-and-macrogenes.qmd) wrote no root-level hierarchical orthogroups. Here the root is Choanozoa and **node N1 = Metazoa**, so the Metazoa-level groups exist (`N1.tsv`).
- **137,235 genes (one protein per gene), 85.6% in 13,282 orthogroups:**
  - 3,255 orthogroups contain all seven species;
  - 1,260 are single-copy in every species (@tbl-overall).
- **Gene placement follows divergence and genome history** (@fig-overview):
  - human and zebrafish have 93% of genes in orthogroups;
  - *Mnemiopsis*, fly and *Ciona* 78–80%;
  - oyster has 31.5% of its genes in oyster-only orthogroups, the most of any species. Its branch carries 16,601 gene duplications.
- **One-to-one orthologs:** human–zebrafish 9,208 pairs; *Mnemiopsis* pairs 3,062–4,384. Oyster–*Ciona* (5,607) has more than *Ciona*–zebrafish (4,055), because zebrafish genes are often duplicated.
- **Two gene-level reference tables for the SATURN benchmarks:**
  - orthogroups: 29,292 groups;
  - Metazoa-level groups: 30,275 groups.
:::

# Key terms

| Term | Meaning here |
|---|---|
| **Orthogroup (OG)** | All genes descended from one gene in the last common ancestor of the species analysed (orthologs plus in-paralogs). |
| **Hierarchical orthogroup (HOG)** | An orthogroup defined at one node of the species tree using gene trees. A HOG at the Metazoa node holds the genes descended from one gene in the last common ancestor of animals. Duplications older than that node split groups. |
| **Outgroup** | A species outside the group of interest, used to root the tree. Here *S. rosetta*, a choanoflagellate (the closest living relatives of animals). |
| **Species-specific orthogroup** | An orthogroup containing genes from only one species, typically a lineage-specific family or expansion. |
| **Unassigned gene** | A gene placed in no orthogroup: no detectable relative among the other proteomes. |
| **One-to-one orthologs** | A gene pair where each species has exactly one copy descended from the ancestral gene. |
| **Gene duplication (per node)** | A duplication event OrthoFinder places on a branch of the species tree from the gene trees. |

: Terms used in this entry. {#tbl-terms}

# 1. Why a new run

- **Fly and human are new.** The eggNOG annotation tables and the Oct 15 OrthoFinder run cover only the original four species.
- **Metazoa-level HOGs were missing.**
  - The Oct 15 run used a fixed tree with *Mnemiopsis* at the base, so the Metazoa node was the root.
  - OrthoFinder 3.1 wrote no `N0.tsv` (root-level HOGs). That left only orthogroups, which can lump paralogs from very old duplications.
  - Adding a non-animal outgroup puts the Metazoa node one step below the root.
- ***S. rosetta*** has a well-annotated RefSeq proteome (~11.6k genes) and is a standard choanoflagellate outgroup.

# 2. Inputs

One protein per gene: the longest. Gene IDs use the same protein-to-gene bridges as the SATURN embeddings (`06a`). Internal stop codons are replaced by X.

| Species | Proteome | Genes | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| *Mnemiopsis leidyi* | genome-v3 gene models | 15,545 | as on Oct 15 |
| *Crassostrea gigas* (oyster) | NCBI RefSeq | 31,371 | as on Oct 15 |
| *Ciona robusta* | Ghost KY21 | 18,788 | as on Oct 15 |
| *Danio rerio* (zebrafish) | Ensembl 113 GRCz11 | 25,400 | as on Oct 15 (unnamed alternate-haplotype copies dropped) |
| *Drosophila melanogaster* (fly) | Ensembl 113 BDGP6.46 | 13,986 | |
| *Homo sapiens* (human) | Ensembl 113 GRCh38 | 20,527 | **primary assembly only:** 11,512 proteins (3,337 genes) on alternate-haplotype (HSCHR\*) and patch (HG\*) scaffolds dropped; 98% duplicate a primary-assembly gene and would otherwise look like paralogs. Unplaced primary scaffolds (KI\*, GL\*) kept |
| *Salpingoeca rosetta* (outgroup) | NCBI RefSeq GCF_000188695.1 | 11,618 | 11,725 proteins, all linked to a gene via GFF `locus_tag` |
| **Total** | | **137,235** | |

: OrthoFinder input (one longest protein per gene). {#tbl-input}

# 3. The run

- **Command:** OrthoFinder 3.1.0, `-M msa -A mafft -T fasttree -t 16 -a 16`.
- **Species tree:** `(Sros,(Mlei,((Cgig,Dmel),(Crob,(Drer,Hsap)))))`, fixed with `-s`.
  - It assumes ctenophores branch first among animals. With a single ctenophore and no sponge, the sponge-first hypothesis gives the same Metazoa node.
- **Compute:** Pegasus `parallel` queue (one 16-core node).
  - 4.3 h (15,617 s), 56 CPU-hours.
  - Peak memory 41.5 GB.
  - The 4-species run took 70 min and 15.9 GB.
- **Node labels assigned by OrthoFinder:**

| Node | Clade | Species below it | HOG file |
|---|---|---|---|
| N0 | Choanozoa (root) | all 7 | not written (OrthoFinder 3.1 does not output the root) |
| **N1** | **Metazoa** | 6 SATURN species | `N1.tsv` |
| N2 | Bilateria | oyster, fly, *Ciona*, zebrafish, human | `N2.tsv` |
| N3 | Protostomia | oyster, fly | `N3.tsv` |
| N4 | Deuterostomia | *Ciona*, zebrafish, human | `N4.tsv` |
| N5 | Vertebrata | zebrafish, human | `N5.tsv` |

: Species-tree nodes. {#tbl-nodes}

# 4. Results

## 4.1 Overall

| Statistic | 6 species + outgroup (this run) | 4 species (Oct 15) |
|---|---|---|
| Genes | 137,235 | 91,104 |
| Genes in orthogroups | 117,535 (85.6%) | 75,861 (83.3%) |
| Unassigned genes | 19,700 (14.4%) | 15,243 (16.7%) |
| Orthogroups | 13,282 (mean 8.8, median 6 genes) | 12,254 (mean 6.2, median 4) |
| Species-specific orthogroups | 3,543, holding 22,876 genes (16.7%) | 3,561, holding 22,576 genes (24.8%) |
| Orthogroups with all species | 3,255 | 4,987 |
| … single-copy in every species | 1,260 | 2,577 |
| G50 / O50 (assigned genes) | 11 genes / 2,085 orthogroups | 5 genes / 3,263 orthogroups |

: OrthoFinder summary statistics. {#tbl-overall}

Orthogroups present in all species and single-copy orthogroups both fall with more species. Each extra species is another chance for a family to be lost or duplicated.

| Species in the orthogroup | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Orthogroups | 3,543 | 1,814 | 792 | 878 | 1,220 | 1,780 | 3,255 |

: Orthogroups by number of species. {#tbl-span}

## 4.2 Per species

| | *Mnemiopsis* | oyster | fly | *Ciona* | zebrafish | human | *S. rosetta* |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Genes | 15,545 | 31,371 | 13,986 | 18,788 | 25,400 | 20,527 | 11,618 |
| % in orthogroups | 78.5 | 90.8 | 79.8 | 77.6 | 93.3 | 93.3 | 71.0 |
| % in species-specific orthogroups | 20.1 | **31.5** | 14.2 | 15.6 | 7.1 | 6.9 | 14.9 |
| % unassigned | 21.5 | 9.2 | 20.2 | 22.4 | 6.7 | 6.7 | 29.0 |
| Orthogroups containing the species | 6,308 | 9,156 | 6,194 | 7,468 | 9,014 | 8,951 | 5,533 |
| Duplications on its own branch | 4,681 | **16,601** | 3,625 | 5,106 | 8,537 | 4,425 | 2,400 |

: Per-species statistics (genes = one protein per gene). {#tbl-perspecies}

![Left: share of each species' genes in multi-species orthogroups, species-specific orthogroups, or unassigned. Right: one-to-one ortholog pairs between each pair of species.](/images/20261020_orthofinder_6sp_overview.png){#fig-overview}

- **Vertebrates are the best connected:** 86% of human and zebrafish genes are in multi-species orthogroups. That reflects their gene content and their mutual closeness: the panel has two vertebrates and one of each other lineage.
- ***Mnemiopsis*, fly and *Ciona*** have about a fifth of their genes unassigned. For *Mnemiopsis* this caps any orthology-based score: genes without a detectable relative cannot be judged right or wrong by an orthology reference.
- **Oyster stands out.** 31.5% of its genes are in oyster-only orthogroups, and its branch carries more duplications (16,601) than any other. That fits the known lineage-specific gene family expansions in oysters.
- **Zebrafish** has the second-highest branch duplication count (8,537), consistent with the teleost genome duplication.

## 4.3 One-to-one orthologs

| | *Mnemiopsis* | oyster | fly | *Ciona* | zebrafish | human |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| *Mnemiopsis* | | 4,245 | 3,546 | 4,384 | 3,062 | 3,292 |
| oyster | | | 4,549 | 5,607 | 4,085 | 4,333 |
| fly | | | | 4,531 | 3,368 | 3,273 |
| *Ciona* | | | | | 4,055 | 4,303 |
| zebrafish | | | | | | **9,208** |

: One-to-one ortholog pairs between the six SATURN species. {#tbl-o2o}

- **Human–zebrafish is by far the richest pair** (9,208), which makes it the natural positive control for cross-species cell matching.
- **Every *Mnemiopsis* pair has 3,000–4,400 one-to-one orthologs**: fewest with the vertebrates, most with *Ciona* and oyster.
- **Oyster–*Ciona* (5,607) exceeds *Ciona*–zebrafish (4,055),** although *Ciona* and zebrafish are the closer relatives. Duplications on the zebrafish lineage turn many one-to-one relationships into one-to-many; the same was seen with four species on Oct 15.

## 4.4 Duplications on internal branches

| Node | Duplications (all) | Duplications (≥50% support) |
|---|---|---|
| N1 Metazoa | 1,047 | 591 |
| N2 Bilateria | 1,340 | 680 |
| N3 Protostomia | 93 | 93 |
| N4 Deuterostomia | 200 | 171 |
| N5 Vertebrata | 4,251 | 4,251 |

: Gene duplications placed on internal branches of the species tree. {#tbl-dups}

The vertebrate stem carries most internal-branch duplications, as expected from the two vertebrate whole-genome duplications. Only 591 well-supported duplications sit at the Metazoa node, so most Metazoa-level HOGs match their orthogroup.

## 4.5 Reference tables for the SATURN benchmarks

`06c` turns the output into gene-level tables (species, gene, protein, group) with the outgroup removed. It finds the Metazoa node automatically from the species tree: the node whose descendants are exactly the six species.

| Table | Groups (incl. singletons) | Genes in groups of ≥2 | Genes in groups with all 6 species |
|---|---|---|---|
| Orthogroups (`ALL6_gene_orthofinder_OG.csv`) | 29,292 | 109,141 (87% of 125,617) | 46,272 (37%) |
| Metazoa HOGs (`ALL6_gene_orthofinder_N1HOG.csv`) | 30,275 | 108,798 | 41,426 (33%) |

: Gene-level reference tables (six SATURN species). {#tbl-tables}

The HOG table splits orthogroups at duplications older than Metazoa, so it is the stricter reference: fewer groups span all six species. Both will be used to score the 6-species SATURN macrogene runs.

# Caveats

- **Fixed species tree, ctenophores first.** HOG levels depend on it. With one ctenophore and no sponge the Metazoa node is the same under either hypothesis.
- **Annotation quality differs between species.** *Mnemiopsis* and *Ciona* gene models are less complete than human or fly, which raises their unassigned share. Gene-model completeness (e.g. BUSCO) would make the comparison fairer.
- **One protein per gene (longest).** Other isoforms can carry different domains; this matches standard OrthoFinder practice.
- **Peak memory (41.5 GB) exceeded the 32 GB requested.** It fitted only because the node had 62.8 GB. Request ≥48 GB for runs this size.
